title: Palindromic Substrings
oneLinerQuestion: Count how many total palindromic substrings exist in a given string.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Palindromic Substrings problem asks for the total number of substrings within a given string that read the same forwards and backwards. Checking all O(N^2) possible substrings takes O(N^3) time using naive validation. We can optimize this to O(N^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space using the 'Expand Around Center' technique. A palindrome is symmetric around its center. In a string of length N, there are exactly 2N - 1 candidate centers: N single-character centers representing odd-length palindromes (centered at index i) and N - 1 two-character centers representing even-length palindromes (centered between index i and i + 1). By expanding two pointers outward simultaneously from each candidate center as long as the boundary characters match, each successful match identifies an additional valid palindromic substring.

- Step 1: Counter Initialization — We initialize an accumulator variable `count = 0` to maintain the total count of valid palindromic substrings found.

- Step 2: Center Expansion Helper Definition — We define a helper function `countPalindromes(s, left, right)`: while `left >= 0`, `right < s.length`, and `s[left] === s[right]`, we increment a local counter `res++` (or directly increment the global `count++`), then expand outward by decrementing `left--` and incrementing `right++`. When the loop terminates, return `res`.

- Step 3: Candidate Centers Traversal — We iterate through string `s` from index `i = 0` to `s.length - 1`, treating index `i` as the root of both odd and even expansion configurations.

- Step 4: Odd-Length Palindrome Expansion — For each index `i`, we expand around the single-character center `(i, i)`: `count += countPalindromes(s, i, i)`. Every match found (beginning with the single character itself) contributes to the running total.

- Step 5: Even-Length Palindrome Expansion — For each index `i`, we expand around the adjacent two-character boundary `(i, i + 1)`: `count += countPalindromes(s, i, i + 1)`. Matches are counted as long as the adjacent characters and subsequent outward boundaries remain identical.

- Step 6: Termination & Total Return — Once all 2N - 1 candidate centers have completed their outward expansions, `count` contains the total number of distinct palindromic substrings across the entire string. We return `count`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N^2) where N is the length of string `s`, since there are 2N - 1 centers and each expansion takes at most O(N) comparisons in the worst case (e.g., strings consisting of all identical characters). Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space, requiring only a few integer pointers and counter variables without additional memory allocation.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION countSubstrings(s):
    res = 0
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        res = res + countPalindromes(s, i, i)
        res = res + countPalindromes(s, i, i + 1)
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION countPalindromes(s, l, r):
    count = 0
    WHILE l >= 0 AND r < LENGTH(s) AND s[l] == s[r] DO:
        count = count + 1; l = l - 1; r = r + 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN count
END FUNCTION
